title: NHS England South East Rolls Out Skin Analytics' AI Skin Cancer Checks in the Largest Deployment of Autonomous Medical AI in NHS History
source_used: Business Wire (Skin Analytics release), read on Enid News copy
key_facts: DERM, developed by Skin Analytics, will go live throughout all 18 NHS South East Trusts from autumn 2026.
AI will be used to triage (sort by urgency) skin cancer referrals across the South East region.
The company says the rollout extends fast, accurate skin cancer detection to a further 9 million people.
The company calls it the largest roll out of autonomous medical AI in NHS history.
The release does not say how the AI decisions are checked by clinicians or give accuracy figures.
quote_evidence: AI will be used to triage skin cancer referrals across the whole of the NHSE South East region, in the largest roll out of autonomous medical AI in NHS history.
DERM, developed by Skin Analytics, will go live throughout all 18 NHS South East Trusts from autumn, extending fast, accurate skin cancer detection of a further 9 million people.
why_it_matters_hint: A large AI rollout for skin cancer referrals, with the speed, accuracy and autonomy claims made by the company.
notes: Original Business Wire page returned HTTP 000 (blocked here). The Enid News copy carries the release text, which is short. Enid News is a copy site, so the source is credited as Business Wire (the release). The release does not say what 'autonomous' means in practice; this is the company's term.
